region.harbourside.desc: Cranes, salt air and four streets that know everyone's business.
region.old_town.desc: Older money, narrower streets, longer memories.
region.eastfield.desc: Warehouses and half-built lots on the edge of the map.
skill.persuasion.desc: Getting people to agree without making them feel pushed.
skill.intimidation.desc: Making someone believe the easy path is the one you offered.
skill.haggling.desc: Moving a price without souring the room.
skill.observation.desc: Noticing what people would rather you didn't.
skill.streetwise.desc: Knowing how things actually work around here.
skill.first_aid.desc: Stopping bleeding, setting bones, keeping someone calm.
skill.brawling.desc: Close fighting, mostly ugly and mostly short.
skill.labour.desc: Lifting, loading and lasting a full shift.
skill.endurance_training.desc: Staying on your feet longer than the other person.
skill.lockpicking.desc: Opening what was closed to you.
skill.repair.desc: Fixing what is broken, or making it look fixed.
skill.cooking.desc: Turning cheap ingredients into a real meal.
background.returning.desc: You grew up on these streets and left. Nobody has decided yet whether they are glad you are back.
background.dockhand.desc: Strong hands, a standing job and very little in the bank. The crew knows your name.
background.in_debt.desc: You talked your way into this and you will have to talk your way out. Someone is counting the days.
background.trained.desc: Training that is worth something anywhere, and a reason you are not using it here.

opening.bg_returning.1: Eleven years since you left Harbourside. The cranes have not moved. The people have.
opening.bg_returning.2: Ida at the corner shop still knows your face. She has not decided yet what she thinks of it.
opening.bg_returning.3: The flat on Dock Street is small, and it is yours, and the rent is due.
opening.bg_dockhand.1: Six days a week the harbour owns your hands. On the seventh it lends them back.
opening.bg_dockhand.2: Veikko says more moves through Warehouse 9 than anybody writes down.
opening.bg_dockhand.3: The boats are late this morning. For once, the morning is yours.
opening.bg_in_debt.1: You borrowed from Rauno because it was easy. Paying it back will not be.
opening.bg_in_debt.2: Twenty in your pocket, and a promise you made in a voice you did not mean.
opening.bg_in_debt.3: He knows where you live. Around here, everybody does.
opening.bg_trained.1: The certificate is on the wall. The reason you left the hospital is in a box under the bed.
opening.bg_trained.2: Sanna at the clinic keeps asking whether you would cover a shift.
opening.bg_trained.3: Harbourside does not need to know why you came. Not yet.
opening.fallback.1: You have lived in Harbourside long enough to be part of it, and not long enough to be sure of it.
opening.common.last: Seven in the morning. Outside, Harbourside is waking up.
ui.msg.refused.on_their_way: They're on their way somewhere and don't stop.
dialogue.generic.about_self.1: Just someone who lives around here.
dialogue.generic.about_work.1: Oh, this and that. Nothing worth telling.
dialogue.generic.about_place.1: {place}? It's here in Harbourside. You'll find it.
dialogue.generic.hired.1: Alright, you're on. Come in for the next shift, and don't be late.
dialogue.generic.not_hiring.1: I've got no work for you, sorry.
dialogue.generic.not_qualified.1: I can't take you on for this. You'd need the training — or the papers.
dialogue.generic.do_not_know_you.1: I don't know you. Come by a few more times first.
dialogue.generic.already_hired.1: You already work here. See you at your shift.
dialogue.generic.compliment.2: That's kind of you to say.
dialogue.generic.flirt_welcome.1: You're sweet. Careful, I might get used to it.
dialogue.generic.flirt_unwelcome.1: Let's keep it friendly, shall we?
dialogue.generic.insult.2: You can say that somewhere else.
dialogue.generic.threaten.1: I think you should go. Now.
dialogue.generic.threaten.2: I'm not talking to you any more.
dialogue.generic.gift_accepted.1: {amount}? I — thank you. I won't forget it.
dialogue.generic.gift_no_cash.1: You don't have that on you. Don't play games with me.
dialogue.npc_ida.greet.1: Buying, or asking? Either way, be quick about it.
dialogue.npc_ida.greet.2: Mm. You again, or someone who looks like you.
dialogue.npc_ida.about_self.1: Ida. Lahtinen, like it says over the door. My father opened this shop and I've kept it open since.
dialogue.npc_ida.about_work.1: Tins, bread, cigarettes, stamps. Everyone owes me for something, and I know exactly how much.
dialogue.npc_ida.unknown.1: I don't follow. Say it plainer.
dialogue.npc_ida.unknown.2: Is that a question, or just talk?
dialogue.npc_ida.farewell.1: Mind the step on your way out.
dialogue.npc_elias.greet.1: Hey. You look like someone who knows where the money is.
dialogue.npc_elias.greet.2: Oh — hi. Don't tell my mother you saw me here.
dialogue.npc_elias.about_self.1: Elias. Ida's son, if you're wondering why she glares at me. Between jobs. It's a long between.
dialogue.npc_elias.about_work.1: Work? I've got plans. Plans are work, if you do them right.
dialogue.npc_elias.unknown.1: Sorry, I was miles away. What was that?
dialogue.npc_veikko.greet.1: All right. Shift's long, so talk while I stand here.
dialogue.npc_veikko.about_self.1: Veikko. Twenty-two years on these docks. Knees say forty.
dialogue.npc_veikko.about_work.1: Loading, unloading, waiting for boats that are late. Warehouse 9 pays better than it should, and nobody asks why.
dialogue.npc_veikko.farewell.1: See you at the Anchor, maybe.
dialogue.npc_tuomas.greet.1: What'll it be? Drink or conversation. One of them's free.
dialogue.npc_tuomas.greet.2: It's evening in here whatever the clock says. Sit.
dialogue.npc_tuomas.about_self.1: Tuomas. I pour, I listen, I forget. The forgetting's the part people pay for.
dialogue.npc_tuomas.about_work.1: Keeping the Anchor afloat. Harder than it sounds, with this crowd.
dialogue.npc_tuomas.unknown.1: I've heard stranger things tonight. Not many.
dialogue.npc_sanna.greet.1: Hello. Are you hurt, or just visiting? Both are allowed.
dialogue.npc_sanna.greet.2: Hi. Sit down a moment, you look like you've been on your feet all day.
dialogue.npc_sanna.about_self.1: Sanna. I run the clinic, mostly on coffee and good intentions.
dialogue.npc_sanna.about_work.1: Stitches from the docks, coughs from the damp, and more bruises than anyone explains.
dialogue.npc_sanna.unknown.1: Sorry — long shift. Could you say that again?
dialogue.npc_sanna.farewell.1: Take care of yourself. I mean it.
dialogue.npc_marika.greet.1: Good day. Something I can help you with?
dialogue.npc_marika.greet.2: I've seen you around. Everything in order?
dialogue.npc_marika.about_self.1: Constable Aalto. Harbourside's my beat, and has been for longer than it's been quiet.
dialogue.npc_marika.about_work.1: Keeping the peace. Writing things down. People forget; paper doesn't.
dialogue.npc_marika.unknown.1: I'm not sure what you're asking me.
dialogue.npc_rauno.greet.1: Well. A new face. New faces are either trouble or opportunity.
dialogue.npc_rauno.greet.2: You want something. Everyone who comes this way does.
dialogue.npc_rauno.about_self.1: Rauno. I help people get what they need. What they owe me afterwards is between us.
dialogue.npc_rauno.about_work.1: Import, export. Mostly the part in between.
dialogue.npc_rauno.unknown.1: Say what you mean. I don't write things down, so I listen carefully.
dialogue.npc_rauno.farewell.1: We'll talk again. We always do.
dialogue.npc_pirjo.greet.1: Oh, hello, dear! Come closer, my eyes aren't what they were.
dialogue.npc_pirjo.greet.2: There you are. I was just thinking about the old harbour. Were you?
dialogue.npc_pirjo.about_self.1: Pirjo Salo. I've lived here since the cranes were wooden. Sanna lets me keep her company.
dialogue.npc_pirjo.about_work.1: Work! Forty years at the fish hall. Now I supervise the street from my window.
dialogue.npc_pirjo.unknown.1: What's that, dear? Speak up a little.
dialogue.npc_pirjo.farewell.1: Come and visit. I'll tell you about the storm of '79.
dialogue.npc_joonas.about_self.1: Joonas. I work the docks with Veikko.
dialogue.npc_joonas.about_work.1: Heavy lifting. The pay goes home, mostly.
dialogue.npc_leena.greet.1: Hi hi! Coffee? You look like a coffee person.
dialogue.npc_leena.greet.2: Oh good, a new face! Sit, sit — have you heard what happened at the Anchor?
dialogue.npc_leena.about_self.1: Leena! I run Kaisla. Best cinnamon buns on the harbour, and the best view of everyone's business.
dialogue.npc_leena.about_work.1: Coffee, buns, and listening. Mostly listening.
dialogue.npc_leena.unknown.1: Ha! I love it. I have no idea what you mean, but I love it.
dialogue.npc_leena.farewell.1: Come back soon — I'll have news!
